maya_intro.title: Necessary Distance
maya_intro.narrator: Maya Itho. Scientist. What she chose to tell.
maya_intro.text:
People have often criticized my calm. As if feeling less intensely meant understanding less well.

It is the opposite.

Distance is what lets you see clearly, without fear distorting what you look at.

That night, I needed every bit of distance I was capable of.

choices.text: You hide what you feel very well.
You just have a different way of coping.

maya_metier.title: The Laboratory
maya_metier.text:
I've been a biologist on Aletheia-9 for two years, studying samples brought back by probes from the system.

My laboratory is my real command center, even if no one calls it that.

Three weeks before Léo's disappearance, a probe brought back a sample taken from a cometary fragment.

Nothing officially extraordinary. On paper.

maya_echantillon.title: Sample 7
maya_echantillon.text:
I called it Sample 7, for simplicity.

A crystalline structure, apparently inert, but with a slight bioluminescent reaction to certain electrical frequencies.

It was not in the mission protocol to study it beyond the bare minimum. I did it anyway, on my own time.

I should have reported it officially. I did not.

choices.text: Do you regret not reporting it?

maya_decouverte.title: One Week Before
maya_decouverte.text:
Five days before the incident, the sample reacted unusually: a rhythmic light pulse, almost regular, in response to a simple current variation in my laboratory.

I noted the observation in my personal journal. Not in the official report.

I wanted to understand before alarming anyone for nothing. That's what I told myself, anyway.

choices.text: You were mostly afraid of the consequences.

maya_nuit_debut.title: 02:00 — Laboratory
maya_nuit_debut.text:
That night, I was in my laboratory, Sample 7 under its display case, monitoring its variations as I had every evening for a week.

Léo stopped by to see me late in the evening, before heading to maintenance.

He asked, almost shyly, if he could see *"the stone that glows."* He'd heard about it through corridor rumor.

choices.text: Léo seemed innocent in all of this.

maya_leo.title: Léo
maya_leo.text:
I showed him, briefly. He stood fascinated before the display case, almost hypnotized by the rhythm of the pulses.

*"It's like it's breathing"*, he said.

He asked me a lot of questions, more than usual. About its origin, about what it might be.

Then he left for sector 4 for his routine check, a little after 01:50.

maya_coupure.title: 02:13 — The Coincidence
maya_coupure.text:
At 02:13, the exact moment the alarm sounded, Sample 7 emitted a light spike more intense than I had ever measured.

Almost at the same instant as the power outage in sector 4, at the other end of the station.

A coincidence. Surely. Coincidences exist, in science.

But this one chilled me.

choices.text: You immediately wanted to warn someone.
You first thought of protecting your research.

maya_choix.title: A Quick Decision
maya_choix.text:
I hesitated, for only a few seconds, before heading to the command center.

I did not mention the sample at that moment. Only the outage, like everyone else.

I told myself it was probably not related. That mentioning it would only sow confusion.

I'm no longer sure that was the right reason.

choices.text: You should have spoken up right away.

maya_confinement.title: The Descent
maya_confinement.text:
Rhea asked me to accompany her to sector 4, once the lockdown was lifted.

Dorian wanted to go down alone, earlier, but Rhea insisted it be me, because of my technical knowledge of energy anomalies.

I said nothing about the sample, neither during the trip nor on site.

choices.text: You already knew what you would find.

maya_scene_vide.title: A Familiar Trace
maya_scene_vide.text:
The open panel, the tools on the floor, no trace of Léo: I saw all of that like the others.

But I noticed something else, near the electrical panel: a fine crystalline residue, almost invisible, that matched exactly the structure of Sample 7.

I did not report it to anyone at the time.

I discreetly collected it, to analyze alone, later.

maya_secret.title: What I Still Haven't Said
maya_secret.text:
I never officially declared Sample 7, its strange reactions, or that trace found near the panel.

Part of me was afraid they would forbid my research. Another part, more honest, was afraid of being right.

If this sample has a link to Léo's disappearance, then I carry a responsibility I have not yet found the courage to fully accept.

maya_conclusion.title: My Version
maya_conclusion.text:
I do not believe in human sabotage. I do not believe in a simple technical failure either.

I believe something happened that night that we do not yet fully understand — something linked to what I have been studying in secret for three weeks.

I cannot tell you where Léo is. But I can tell you I have not told everything, until now.

fin_recit_maya.title: End of Account
fin_recit_maya.text: Maya's account ends. For the first time since your arrival, her voice trembled, just barely.
